first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 revenue $244.5-245.5M and non-GAAP EPS ~$0.18 (company guide, Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001544522/000154452226000135/q226quarterlyearningsrelea.htm). Consensus is $244.9M per MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/freshworks-nasdaqfrsh-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-04/) and ~$245.06M / $0.18 per The Stock Observer (https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8967169). The guide and two agreeing estimates make the bar sourced. One MarketBeat EPS figure of $0.15 is an outlier. Non-GAAP operating income guide is $59-61M. FY26 guide is $963.5-966.5M revenue and $222-228M non-GAAP operating income. No sourced consensus exists for the Q4 guide or a 2027 first look.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 29,267,192 shares, 12.26% of float, days to cover 2.9, report date 2026-10-15, published 2026-10-26. That is up 17.1% from 24,987,927 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/FRSH/short-interest/). Shorts were building while the stock made a 52-week high of about $15.45 around Oct 21-23. Options (baseline): 25d skew -9.0 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.12, event-implied move 14.63% against a median own reaction of 3.0%, ATM spread 27% of mid. Spot $14.20 is 8% below the 52-week high, 106% above the 52-week low, -4.7% over 5 days and +3.2% over 20 days. The short is crowded-ish but not at the 18-23% squeeze levels, and the options market leans up.

evidence.text: ServiceNow, the ITSM category leader, reported Q3 on 2026-10-28 after the close. It guided Q4 cRPO growth to 18.5% against roughly 19.8% expected, and the shares fell about 15-18% after hours and premarket, even though revenue beat ($4.11B vs $4.10B) and subscription revenue grew 21%. This is the first large ITSM print since Freshworks last spoke on Aug 4, and it resets sentiment on forward ITSM bookings and guides into FRSH's Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FRSH fell 16.4% when its forward guide disappointed (Feb 2026 print, FY26 guide $952-960M amid a software selloff; https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/02/15/why-freshworks-stock-plummeted-this-week/). It fell 4.3% after its Aug 2026 beat-and-raise.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FRSH is -4.7% over 5 sessions, which covers the NOW print. If the market had fully transmitted NOW's -17% to an ITSM peer, FRSH's put skew would be bid. Instead the 25d skew is -9 (upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.12. NOW's management blamed company-specific causes (renewals pulled into Q3, on-prem mix, T4C exclusions from backlog), so the transmission to a mid-market vendor is a proxy that FRSH has not confirmed.
evidence.independence: The cRPO detail is from a second outlet: https://aiweekly.co/alerts/servicenow-shares-sink-15-after-hours-as-q4-crpo-guide-lands-below-street. Both describe one event. It is a peer proxy, not a Freshworks number.

evidence.text: Freshworks has beaten its revenue guide for seven straight quarters (CFO, Q2 call). Q2 revenue was $237.4M against $233.6M consensus (+1.6%) and above the top of its range. Q3 is guided at $244.5-245.5M with consensus about $245M, so a repeat lands near $248M, roughly +1.2% over the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are sold: 6 of the last 7 prints closed down. Q2 2026 (revenue +1.6% vs consensus, FY raised) went -4.32%; Q1 2026 (beat) -3.26%; Q3 2025 (beat) -1.90%. Only Apr 2025 was up (+3.0%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat of the guide is what the street expects from this company, and the reaction history shows the market does not pay for it. The only unpriced part is the size of the beat against a consensus that sits mid-guide.
evidence.independence: The Q2 consensus comparison is from MarketBeat: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/freshworks-nasdaqfrsh-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-04/. The beat pattern itself comes from the company's own document.

evidence.text: The May 2026 restructuring cut about 500 roles, 11% of the workforce, and was substantially complete by end-Q2. The CFO said Q2's non-GAAP operating income of $55.9M (23.6% margin, 'well above estimates') reflected only the 'partial impact of restructuring savings', so Q3 carries the first full quarter of savings against an operating income guide of $59-61M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's large operating income beat and FY operating income raise ($207-215M to $222-228M) met a -4.32% reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide: the Aug raise of the FY operating income guide already reflected the savings, and the CFO said leverage is being reinvested in EX sales and AI R&D. Only an operating income print well above $61M would be new.
evidence.independence: The 'partial impact' wording is from the Q2 call transcript (https://s21.q4cdn.com/987526491/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Freshworks_Q2_2026_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf), a different document from the same company.

evidence.text: The $400M buyback authorized Feb 25, 2026 had about $195.6M left at June 30 after $159M was spent in Q2 alone (18.3M shares). At the Q2 pace the authorization is largely used up by Q3 end, and the company holds $665M cash with no debt. A new or expanded authorization alongside the Q3 print is plausible.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $400M authorization was announced Feb 26, 2026, outside an earnings print, after the Feb -16% reaction. No clean print-day reaction to a buyback is on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: Remaining capacity is in the 10-Q but not on any preview found. If a re-authorization were expected, it would show in preview commentary, and none was found. The Q3 share-count guide (266M weighted vs 273M FY) already implies continued buying, so only a new, larger program adds anything.
evidence.independence: The authorization is confirmed in the company's own release: https://ir.freshworks.com/files/doc_news/Freshworks-Announces-Board-Authorization-of-400-Million-Share-Repurchase-Program-2026.pdf. The Q2 pace is on the call transcript.

evidence.text: Short interest rose 17.1% in the second half of September to 29.3M shares (12.26% of float, 2.9 days to cover, as of 2026-10-15). Shorts were adding while the stock pushed to a 52-week high, and call open interest dwarfs puts (P/C OI 0.12).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has been recorded on this name. The stock has roughly doubled off its 52-week low while short interest climbed.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sign is ambiguous. Rising shorts are bears adding into the print, but a 12% short on a print that holds the guide is fuel for a squeeze. The options market already leans up (skew -9), so part of this is in the price.
evidence.independence: Skew and P/C OI come from the sealed baseline (yahoo options), a different source from the FINRA-based short register.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call the CEO said AI Agent Studio for Freshservice (launched May, 1,000+ customers on it) was not yet priced and 'the intention is to price in the fall', on a session-based model. That makes the Q3 call the likely venue for a new AI monetization announcement or a first contribution to the outlook.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Freddy AI attach metrics (Copilot on >70% of larger deals, 7,000+ paying AI customers) were in the Q2 release that was sold -4.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a promise on a call, not in any preview or wire summary found. It matters only if the price point or attach is quantified in a way that moves the 2027 growth view.
evidence.independence: The current CX AI Agent session pricing ($49 per 100 sessions after 500 free) is per pricingsaas: https://pricingsaas.com/companies/freshworks/diffs/2026W20. That is the CX product, not Freshservice.

evidence.text: Freshworks signed on 2026-10-12 to acquire Torii (Israeli SaaS management, $65M raised, terms undisclosed, described as relatively small), closing in Q4. The Q4 guide may carry small acquired revenue and integration opex, plus the first commentary on the deal.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Device42 ($230M, 2024) and FireHydrant were folded in without a print-day reaction on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but its effect on the Q4 operating income guide is not. Tiny in size either way.
evidence.independence: The 'relatively small' characterisation is from a Calcalist summary via https://www.beri.net/article/freshworks-torii-acquisition-ai-spend-governance-freshservice-saas-management-customer-continuity.

evidence.text: Atlassian, which competes in ITSM through Jira Service Management, reported two days after Freshworks last spoke (Aug 6). It said Service Collection ARR crossed $1B, cloud grew 31%, and the stock rose about 35%. That is a peer data point of healthy mid-market ITSM demand, against the ServiceNow signal.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Three months old, so it is in the price. FRSH has since rallied to its 52-week high, partly on the group re-rating. Filed as a small proxy that offsets the ServiceNow read.
evidence.independence: A peer proxy. The guidance detail is in Atlassian's own 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650372/000165037226000031/ex991q4fy26.htm.

evidence.text: Freshworks itself guided Q3 calculated billings growth to about 13% reported (14% cc), below the ~14% revenue growth guide. It said NDR (104% reported, 105% cc) would stay roughly flat in Q3. CX ARR, 41% of total ARR, grows only 3% and is guided to low single digits for FY26. Forward growth is therefore decelerating into the Q4 guide and any 2027 first look, which came with the Q3 print last year (13-14% for 2026).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print, which carried the first full-year guide (~14% growth), fell 16.38%, the largest reaction in the history. In Nov 2025 the preliminary 2026 color was given on the Q3 call and the stock closed -1.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Billings below revenue is in the company's own guide, but the street anchors on revenue. If the deceleration were priced, consensus for 2027 growth would sit visibly below 14%, and no sourced 2027 consensus was found. EX ARR growing mid-20s on 59% of ARR offsets it: total ARR growth needs EX to hold ~24% for the 2027 view to stay at 13-14%.
evidence.independence: Same document as findings 2 and 6 (Q2 call), on a different line (billings/NDR, not revenue beat). The 2026 preliminary color from the Q3 2025 call is per https://ng.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-freshworks-beats-q3-2025-estimates-stock-gains-93CH-2189093 (snippet only, not fetched).

evidence.text: CFO Tyler Sloat had 10,734 shares withheld for tax at $14.72 on 2026-11-01 (code F, RSU vesting) and holds 1,703,156 after. There was no open-market insider selling into the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: n/a
evidence.why_not_priced: Routine and mechanical. Filed so the panel sees that the only pre-print insider filing carries no signal.
evidence.independence: none

The company gives no numerical guidance (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1964789/000110465926090041/tm2621890d1_ex99-1.htm). The bar is disputed, so every finding is capped small. The consensus EPS loss plainly does not model bitcoin fair-value marks.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 18.15M shares as of 2026-10-15, 2.5 days to cover, on 123.26M shares outstanding, which is about 14.7% of shares out (https://massive.com/quote/hut, read 2026-11-03). The same page gave 19.02M shares and 4.5 days to cover at 2026-09-30 in a search snippet; Equibles had 10.06% of float in August. Insiders own about 10.4% (MarketBeat 2026-11-03), so short interest is roughly 16% of float: crowded-ish. Skew +30.69 vol points (25d put IV over call IV), downside heavily paid; put/call OI 0.56; ATM IV 185%. Tape: -30.3% over 20 days and -51.7% from the 52-week high. The stock fell from about $100 in late September to $55.01 on the 2026-11-02 close, then rebounded about 15-16% intraday on 2026-11-03 with miners (RIOT +14%, MARA +9%). On 2026-11-02 KBW cut its target to $92 from $154 (Outperform), warning of a 'lease catalyst drought' through early 2027.

evidence.text: Bitcoin rose 42.71% in Q3 2026 (about $58.5k at the June 30 settle to $83,556 on the Sept 30 Coinbase close). Hut 8 carried about $1.04B of consolidated digital assets at June 30, 2026 ($567.3M in custody, $184.9M pledged for miner purchases, $290.3M pledged as collateral, per the 10-Q). That implies an unrealized digital-asset gain on the order of $350-450M in Q3, against a $138.6M loss in Q2. GAAP net income and EPS should come out strongly positive against a consensus loss of -$0.81 to -$1.25.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-04): a $76.6M gain on digital assets produced $50.6M net income, and the stock fell about 9.65-12.5% that day as BTC fell about 6% (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35884307/hut-8-reports-third-quarter-2025-results). Q2 2026 (2026-08-04): a $138.6M digital-asset loss, EPS -1.27 against -0.55, and the stock fell 9.74% (https://beincrypto.com/hut-8-stock-q2-2026-earnings/). The marks have not been bought.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every published consensus is a loss of $0.81-1.25 a share, so headline EPS will print as a very large 'beat' that screens and algos have not been set up for. The bitcoin price itself is public, and holders who model the mark already know it. If the market had treated the mark as value, the stock would not be down 30% over 20 days while BTC held about $80k+ into mid-October.
evidence.independence: BTC quarter return from a second source: Simple Mining's September 2026 report, Sept close $83,556.14 (https://www.simplemining.io/insights/post/bitcoin-market-report-september-2026). The quarter return is from EdgeX/COINOTAG, 42.71% (https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/bitcoin-q3-2026-best-quarter-since-2017). American Bitcoin held about 8,002 BTC at June 30 (https://www.abtc.com/news-and-insights/american-bitcoin-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). The holdings and the price come from different documents.

evidence.text: The street's bar for new AI/HPC leasing at this print is low: KBW cut its target to $92 from $154 on 2026-11-02 and warned of a 'lease catalyst drought' through early 2027. Yet Hut 8 has announced its largest lease alongside a print before (Q1 2026 on 2026-05-06, a $9.8B Beacon Point lease, stock about +35%). It discloses an approximately 8,660 MW development pipeline beyond 949 MW contracted. Any new lease, or River Bend expansion, announced with the release would hit a market positioned for none.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-05-06: Q1 release paired with a $9.8B, 352 MW Beacon Point lease, stock +33-37% (https://parameter.io/hut-8-hut-stock-soars-37-on-massive-9-8b-texas-ai-data-center-agreement/). The prints with no lease news (2026-08-04 -9.7%, 2026-02-25 -6.6%, 2025-11-04 about -10%) all fell.
evidence.why_not_priced: A covering analyst has just told clients to expect no lease news, and the stock has halved from its high with puts bid. If a lease were priced, the skew would not be +30 vol points and targets would not be getting cut 40%. This is optionality and not a sourced pending deal: I found no document saying a lease is imminent, so it is sized small despite the large upside tail.
evidence.independence: The pipeline and contracted MW are from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1964789/000110465926090041/tm2621890d1_ex99-1.htm). The May reaction is from a separate outlet. No document points to a lease at this print.

evidence.text: Beacon Point Phase 2 (the 352 MW, $9.8B lease signed in July 2026) had no financing at the Q2 release ('evaluating a range of structures'). Phase 1 was funded by $4.25B of IG non-recourse notes, and on 2026-09-24 Hut 8 closed a $1.07B four-year parent revolver with JPMorgan, Citi, Goldman and Morgan Stanley, undrawn at close. An update or closing on Phase 2 financing at the print would de-risk the build. The money funds contracted, investment-grade-tenant capacity, not distress.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean print-day precedent. The Phase 1 financing ($4.25B, June 2026) and the River Bend notes ($3.25B, April 2026) were standalone 8-Ks, not print-day items.
evidence.why_not_priced: The revolver is public and partly priced. Whether Phase 2 project debt is done is not public. If funding risk on the second $9.8B lease had been taken off the table, it would show up as less put skew and fewer target cuts from 'execution/funding' bears like Cipher's convert-driven selloff.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release says Phase 2 financing structures were being evaluated (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1964789/000110465926090041/tm2621890d1_ex99-1.htm). That is a different document from the revolver release.

evidence.text: In the Poolin bankruptcy, Hut 8 was named winning bidder at $140M for the Pyote and Tarbush West Texas sites on 2026-09-23. The court reopened the auction on 2026-09-30 with Hut 8's affiliate as stalking horse at up to $180M ($100M at close plus $80M in AI/cloud milestones). The outcome and terms may be disclosed with the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on this line at a print.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is small next to a roughly $7-8B market cap, and the final status is not public. A finished deal adds powered sites to a pipeline the market is currently discounting.
evidence.independence: The Block, 2026-09-23 (https://theblock.co/news/business/2026-09-23-hut-8-wins-bidding-poolin-texas-data-centers-140-million-offer-416190).

evidence.text: On-chain analysts flagged about 1,966 BTC (about $161M) moving from Hut 8-linked wallets to exchanges and OTC desks in the week to 2026-10-16, and the company made no statement. A Q4 bitcoin sale is likely to be disclosed as a subsequent event or on the call. What it buys is unanswered: the amount fits the $100M Poolin closing payment plus capex, and the parent also has an undrawn $1.07B revolver, so it is not a distress sale.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell about 7.6% intraday on 2026-10-16 when the transfers were reported (same source), so the market has already reacted once.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock sold off on the report. What is not priced is the confirmed use of the proceeds, which management will explain.
evidence.independence: None from a different source on the transfers themselves.

evidence.text: Revenue looks in line at best against a disputed $72.5-75.9M bar. American Bitcoin's Q2 mining revenue was $67.0M on 932 BTC (about $72k realised). Q3 average BTC was roughly similar (Aug average $69,487, Sept average $80,471, July around $60-63k). Network difficulty rose 5.5% in September, and ABTC's reserve rose only about 300 BTC from June 30 to Sept 3. Hut 8 missed revenue consensus in both Q1 2026 ($71M vs $79.4M) and Q2 2026 ($74.9M vs about $79.4M).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue miss: -9.74% (alongside an EPS miss). Q1 2026 revenue miss: +35%, overridden by the lease. Revenue is not the line this stock trades on when lease news is present.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue has run above the print two quarters in a row. Estimates of $75.9M still sit above Q2's $74.9M while realised BTC prices and production look roughly flat. This is a proxy built from BTC averages, not a company number.
evidence.independence: BTC monthly averages and difficulty from Simple Mining (https://www.simplemining.io/insights/post/bitcoin-market-report-september-2026). The 8,300 BTC reserve on 2026-09-03 is from Eric Trump via EdgeX (https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/american-bitcoin-8300-btc-reserve-eric-trump-us-lead).

evidence.text: Q3 is the first full quarter carrying both project note issues: $3.25B of 6.192% River Bend notes closed 2026-04-30, and $4.25B of 6.129% Beacon Point notes priced in June 2026. That is about $115M of coupon a quarter against Q2 interest expense of $51.2M, unless it is capitalised during construction. The size of any interest step-up below the line is unknown.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Q2's $51.2M interest was part of a print that fell 9.7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Capitalisation policy is not disclosed in what I read. Consensus EPS of -$1.06 against Q2's -$1.27 may or may not carry it. This is an inference, and it is swamped by the BTC mark at the GAAP line.
evidence.independence: Note terms are listed on https://massive.com/quote/hut (8-K summaries). This finding shares the Q2 release with findings 2 and 3, but rests on a different number.

evidence.text: Positioning is washed out and short-crowded into the print. The stock fell from about $100 (a director sold at $100.00 on 2026-09-24) to $55.01 on the 2026-11-02 close. Short interest was about 18.15M shares (about 15% of shares out, about 16% of float) at 2026-10-15. The 50-day moving average is $83.46. A quarter with no new negative leaves room for a squeeze, though a +15-16% pre-print rebound on 2026-11-03 used part of it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The stock has fallen on 5 of the last 7 prints despite a rising tape for most of 2025-26.
evidence.why_not_priced: The +30.7 put skew says the option market is positioned for downside. If the washout were fully priced, implied downside would not be bid this hard after a 45% drawdown. The intraday rebound of 2026-11-03 shows part of it is being unwound now, before the window opens at today's close.
evidence.independence: MarketBeat 2026-11-03: 50-day MA $83.46 and insider sale at $100 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-hut-8-nasdaq-hut-stock-jumps-125-time-to-buy-2026-11-03/).

evidence.text: American Bitcoin (ABTC, majority-owned and consolidated) reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-04. Hut 8 consolidates it first, so ABTC's own release and call fall after this bmo window.
evidence.resolves_by: 2026-11-04 (after close; window ends at the 2026-11-04 close)

evidence.text: Navitas beat revenue consensus in each of its last five quarters, Q2 2026 at $10.53m against $9.97m, yet fell the next session after four of the five. The baseline shows five of six prints down, median absolute move 14.1%, including -12.27% after the Q2 beat with a raised Q3 guide. With the Q3 guide at $13.0-14.0m and consensus at the $13.5m midpoint, a revenue beat of about 3-5% is the market's own expectation, and on this name such a beat has been sold.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-27): revenue beat ($10.53m vs $9.97m) and a Q3 guide well above the street's $11.1m, stock -12.27%. Q1 2026 (05-05): beat ($8.6m vs $8.2m), -4.96%. Q4 2025 (02-24): +19.61%, the only up print in six.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The +10 vol-point put skew and the 26% slide since Sep 30 already show the market expects a sold beat. If it were fully priced, the call-heavy OI (put/call 0.41) and a 19% short position building into the print would not both be present. The open element is the reaction function, not the number.
evidence.independence: The baseline's own reaction history (5 of 6 down, sealed from 8-K item 2.02 times) is a different source from TIKR's consensus-beat count and agrees. Benzinga's estimate table (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVTS/earnings-forecasts) shows the same beat pattern of roughly 5-6% per quarter.

evidence.text: Two AI-power peers reported after Navitas last spoke on 2026-07-27, and both were strong on AI data centres. Monolithic Power (2026-10-29): Enterprise Data revenue $506.7m, +33.2% q/q and +164.6% y/y, data-centre growth floor raised to 150% from 130%, stock about +10% after hours. onsemi (2026-11-02): AI data-centre revenue +39% q/q and +175% y/y, and it raised its 2030 AI-DC target. Navitas guided AI infrastructure to about one-third of Q4 sales.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Navitas's moves on AI and Nvidia news have been large and positive (May-June 2026 rally to $34), but the earnings reactions to the AI narrative have been negative on 5 of 6 prints, so the transmission at prints is weak.
evidence.why_not_priced: NVTS fell 5.6% over the five sessions that include the MPWR print and onsemi's release, so its price did not take the read-through. If it had, NVTS would have tracked MPWR's after-hours move rather than sitting at a 26% 20-day drawdown. Net of the rest of the company: Navitas's AI revenue is about $4-5m of a roughly $15m Q4, its big ramps (800V sidecars and compute trays) are dated mid-2027 by its own deck, and the other two-thirds is industrial, energy and remaining consumer. This is a peer proxy, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: onsemi 8-K ex 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001097864/000114036126041580/ef20084671_ex99-1.htm, 2026-11-02) is a separate company and a separate document pointing the same way. Both are proxies, not Navitas numbers.

evidence.text: Monolithic Power said on 2026-10-29 that it began sampling GaN-based products for 800V data-centre architectures alongside its SiC designs. That puts a $1.2bn-a-quarter power supplier into the GaN-for-800V niche that anchors Navitas's thesis, beside Innoscience, which is on Nvidia's 800V partner list and has a signed Google supply agreement (Feb 2026).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on competition explicitly. The 2026-10-16 move of -9.6% (vs SOX -3.8%) was attributed by commentary to Chinese competition among other things.
evidence.why_not_priced: The MPWR GaN-sampling line was buried in a print the street read as an AI-demand beat; no Navitas coverage I found linked them. If it were priced, call Q&A previews would carry it. It reaches the stock only through the call Q&A and share-of-socket questions, so it is small.
evidence.independence: Innoscience in Nvidia's 800V list and in Google's supply chain (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/02/09/news-innoscience-gan-products-break-into-googles-supply-chain/, 2026-02-09) is a different source with the same direction, but it is older and widely known.

evidence.text: Short interest climbed 27% in a month into the print: 40.3m shares (Sep 15), then 47.5m (Sep 30), then 51.1m (Oct 15), about 19% of about 268m shares outstanding, with days to cover 2.8. A short this crowded and building into a binary print adds squeeze fuel if the Q4 guide or 2027 ramp language surprises. The Q4 2025 print squeezed +19.6%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print: +19.61% with about 25-32% of float short at the time (per Trefis and other trackers). The other five prints all fell despite similar short interest.
evidence.why_not_priced: The October build appears in no preview I found, and the baseline does not carry short interest. The sign is ambiguous: the build is also informed bearish positioning, which the skew already reflects. It is filed as a small net positive for the squeeze mechanism only.
evidence.independence: Call-heavy open interest in the baseline (put/call 0.41) is consistent with a crowded short hedged with calls. It comes from a different source (Yahoo options).

evidence.text: At Citi's conference on 2026-09-08, CEO Chris Allexandre described the 800V transition as four stages and 'not a digital switch'. His own July deck dates 800V sidecars to mid-2027 and native 800V compute trays to mid/late 2027 into 2028. So the Q4 and 2027 commentary on the call is likelier to stretch timing than to pull it forward, which is the line this stock trades on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 call (2026-07-27): the guide was raised, the ramp was framed as 2H26-2027, and the stock fell 12.27%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The 26% fall since Sep 30 and the -72% from the June high already reflect a slower ramp. What would still be new is a quantified slip, such as AI share in Q4 below the one-third promised. I found no document showing it, so this is sized small.
evidence.independence: The July investor deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000162828026049795/exhibit992-navitas2q26ea.htm) carries the same staged timeline, so the two share the company as source.

evidence.text: Navitas carries two active suits that can show up in Q3 opex and call Q&A. Renesas sued for trade-secret misappropriation and named CEO Allexandre personally (N.D. Cal. 5:26-cv-07573, 2026-07-22). Wolfspeed sued for patent infringement over GaNFast, GaNSlim, GaNSafe, GeneSiC MOSFETs and SiCPAK (D. Del., 2026-07-07). Navitas countersued Renesas in E.D. Tex. on 2026-08-10.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The suits were part of the July-August drawdown, per TIKR. No print has carried a legal-cost line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The suits are public and priced. What is unpriced is the size of the legal spend, which is likely excluded from non-GAAP. No ruling falls in the window, so this is a below-the-line, call-Q&A item [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Wolfspeed suit: https://www.iam-media.com/article/wolfspeed-sues-navitas-patent-infringement-over-gallium-nitride-and-silicon-carbide-technologies (separate article, same litigation cluster).

evidence.text: The Claros acquisition (integrated voltage regulators; up to $232.8m, about 6.9m shares or $89.7m at closing, plus an earnout capped at about 1.28m shares) closed on 2026-10-06. Management does not expect Claros revenue before about 2028. Its engineering cost therefore lands in the Q4 non-GAAP opex guide, last set at $15.5-17.5m for Q3, with no offsetting revenue, so the Q4 loss guide is likely wider than a pre-deal model.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried an acquisition opex step-up. EPS has been beaten only 2 of the last 8 quarters by one source's count, and the stock trades on revenue and AI narrative more than on opex.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q4 EPS consensus may not include Claros's run-rate, since estimates were set around the July guide. If it were in, Q4 EPS estimates would have moved after Oct 6, and I found no revision. It lands below revenue on a stock that trades on revenue and narrative, so it is small.
evidence.independence: The deal terms are in the 2026-08-25 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000110465926100478/tm2623854d1_8k.htm), the same company as source. TIKR's '2028-2029' Claros revenue timing (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-is-up-12-in-2026-73-off-its-high-is-the-power-wall-pitch-a-buy) is secondary.

evidence.text: Navitas holds $557.4m of cash (2026-06-30) against non-GAAP operating burn of roughly $9-10m a quarter, after $380.7m of ATM sales in May-June at about $22 average. There is no financing need at this print, so the dilution overhang that marked earlier prints is absent. Since July, the money has been spent on Claros (mostly stock), a $5m Magnachip stake (SiC licensing partner, 8-K 2026-09-21), and TSMC buffer inventory secured through 2029+.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May-June ATM sales took place during the run to $34 and the subsequent unwind; prints themselves have not carried an offering.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is filed because the question of what the money buys was asked and answered. The cash funds capacity (TSMC buffer, GF 8-inch GaN) and M&A, not distress, so the sign is a small positive. No ATM is needed in the window.
evidence.independence: Magnachip 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821769/000110465926109125/tm2625807d1_8k.htm, 2026-09-21) and TIKR's ATM figures (https://www.tikr.com/blog/navitas-is-up-12-in-2026-73-off-its-high-is-the-power-wall-pitch-a-buy) are separate documents.

800V sidecar and compute-tray revenue is dated mid-2027 to 2028 by the company's own Q2 deck, and the 1200V SiC JFET line early 2027.

evidence.text: Corsicana is the swing item at this print. In August Riot disclosed a non-binding LOI with one undisclosed tenant for the whole Corsicana site (up to 756 MW of IT capacity; the CEO said it could exceed $1B a year in rent). Management named converting it into a lease as a 2026 priority. No executed lease had been disclosed by 2026-11-03: EDGAR shows no 8-K since 10-14, and that 8-K was a custody agreement. The 8:00 ET 4 Nov call is the first earnings call since the LOI. An executed lease would be the largest positive available; a slipping LOI is a modest negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last big lease announcement came with the Q2 print. On 10 Aug 2026 the 191 MW / $9.1B 20-year lease ran +25% after hours, and the stock closed the next session only +4.33% at $20.24 (https://theblock.co/news/business/2026-08-10-riot-platforms-ai-deal-anthropic-411358). The AMD expansion option in the Q1 print went +7% (https://crypto.news/riot-q1-results-show-bitcoin-pressure-and-ai-data-center-growth/). Lease news pays a fraction of its after-hours pop by the close.
evidence.why_not_priced: Whether the LOI converts by this print is unknown and binary. If the market expected an executed lease, the stock would not be down 38% since 30 Sep with downside skew bid, and the street's 2029-2030 revenue estimates would not have been cut 16-27% (TIKR 10-26). Size is about 20% x +8 close-to-close for a signing, less about 80% x -1 for no signing.
evidence.independence: TIKR 10-26 names a Corsicana update as one of the two things 4 Nov has to show (https://www.tikr.com/blog/riot-platforms-fell-38-since-september-30-and-the-streets-mean-target-now-sits-138-above-it-heres-what-november-4-has-to-show). It does not confirm a signing; none was found anywhere.

evidence.text: The refinancing is overdue. The roughly $180M term loan on AMD's first 25 MW, which management expected to close before 30 Sep, had not been announced by 26 Oct, and no 8-K item 1.01/2.03 has been filed since 14 Aug. The $573M Morgan Stanley delayed-draw bridge for the 191 MW AI-lab build matures 31 Dec 2026, and the refinancing waits on an investment-grade backstop the company has not described. What the money buys: the build for a signed 20-year, $9.1B lease (reported to be Anthropic) plus the AMD capacity, and the CFO says the bridge is fully covered by the tenant. Riot prepaid its $200M Coinbase facility on 21 Sep, releasing 5,821 pledged BTC. A $500M ATM has existed since about March 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print where financing was the headline. The stock fell about 8% in the first week of October and 11.5% on 16 Oct, and the cited causes were sector credit and rate worries plus the bridge maturity, not a company release (TIKR 10-08 and 10-20).
evidence.why_not_priced: The slip is public and the drawdown has partly priced it. The call resolves it in one direction or the other. A signed AMD term loan or a named IG backstop would remove the one execution fear analysts keep citing; another 'in the coming months' would confirm it. If the market had priced a clean resolution, the stock would not sit at the street's lowest target ($13) with puts bid.
evidence.independence: Same facts from another source: https://www.merlintrader.com/?p=20473 (updated 2026-11-02), and EDGAR's filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001167419&type=8-K) shows no financing 8-K after 2026-08-14. Both describe one fact set; count it once.

evidence.text: Bitcoin rose about 42.7% in Q3 2026, from $58,527 at 30 Jun (Riot's own Q2 mark) to about $83,460 at 30 Sep. The September figure is implied by Strategy's $70.82B carrying value on 848,517 BTC. On Riot's 11,380 BTC at 30 Jun, less any coins sold to prepay Coinbase, that is roughly $200-285M of fair-value gain, about $0.55-0.76 a share. GAAP EPS should print well above the -$0.27 to -$0.33 consensus. This is a remeasurement with no path to guidance.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Headline EPS has not driven this stock. Q3 2025 net income was $104.5M (a beat) and the stock fell 6.21%. Q1 2026 EPS was -$1.44 against -$0.33 and the stock rose about 7% (https://www.metatrader.com/de/news/1578919-riots-q1-earnings-miss-estimates-revenues-up-yy-shares-rise). Q2 2026 EPS of -$0.68 missed and the stock closed +4.33% the next session.
evidence.why_not_priced: Everyone knows the BTC price, so the mark itself is priced. What may not be priced is the headline: if the consensus EPS excludes the mark, screens and algos will show a large beat at 07:xx ET. The name's history says that is noise by the close.
evidence.independence: The Q3 BTC gain of +42.71% is from COINOTAG via https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/bitcoin-q3-2026-best-quarter-since-2017 (2026-10-01). evidence.text: A peer read-through landed after Riot last spoke. Cipher Digital reported Q3 2026 on 2 Nov. It amended Barber Lake into a second 10-year term directly with a leading AI lab, adding about $5.2B of rent, and sold $850M of 0.000% converts due 2032. Two weeks after the CoreWeave bond scare (yields briefly above 15% on 14 Oct) and Cantor's cuts to seven AI-data-center names (16 Oct), the convertible market was still open to a Texas ex-miner AI landlord, and AI-lab demand was still being contracted. That bears directly on Riot's refinancing question and its Corsicana LOI.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Riot trades with this group: on 16 Oct RIOT fell 11.48% alongside HUT -10.96% and WULF -7.45% on the Cantor note (TIKR 10-20). CIFR's own reaction to its 2 Nov print was not found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: RIOT is +2.1% over five days. This is a proxy, not a Riot document. Riot has not confirmed its own access to the market, and its backstop is a bank IG structure, not a convertible.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. Sector context for the October sell-off is in https://www.tikr.com/blog/riot-platforms-stock-fell-11-on-october-16-after-cantor-cut-its-target-heres-where-the-stock-could-go (2026-10-20).

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Four of seven verified prior reactions were 6-18% in absolute size. Lease news on 10 Aug faded from +25% after hours to +4.33%, so oversold or euphoric starts have not carried.
evidence.why_not_priced: This goes against the skew, so the size is small. The case that the option market is wrong rests on causes: the drop came from sector credit and rate fear, not from Riot's own numbers. If the market expected a damaging print, the 2027-2028 revenue estimates would have fallen with the price, and they fell only 1.2-1.6% while the stock fell 38%.
evidence.independence: Short-interest figures are snippet_only (curvedtrading, swingtradebot); skew is from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Q3 is the first full quarter of rent on AMD's 25 MW, which was delivered in May. Q2 operating lease revenue was $4.9M at 84% margin, and the AMD contract implies about $8M a quarter for 25 MW. Delivery of the next 10 MW is guided for November 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Data-center revenue debuted at $33.2M in Q1 2026 and the stock rose about 7%. That move was mixed with the news of AMD's expansion option.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It falls inside what the company already disclosed. TIKR flags that a full quarter barely above $4.9M would undermine the rent ramp, so only a shortfall would move the stock.

evidence.text: Revolve filed an 8-K (Item 8.01, filed 2026-10-30) disclosing unauthorized access in which an actor obtained, 'through automated means', the names, contact information, card numbers and expiration dates of customers with saved payment details. Texas breach filings alone list 127,200 affected residents (The Record, 2026-10-30). The company says it expects no material impact, and the call is the first chance for analysts to ask about costs, reserves, card-network fines, litigation and any Q4 conversion hit.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior cyber incident at this company. The stock fell -2.86% on 2026-10-30 (934k shares against a ~695k 20d average) and -1.92% on 2026-11-02 (stockanalysis price history), about -4.7% over two sessions after the disclosure.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the ~4.7% two-day fall is the market's first read. Not yet disclosed are the total count (Texas 127,200 implies a national figure in the high hundreds of thousands to low millions against 3.04M active customers, which is an inference), any Q4 charge, and whether saved-card removal hurts repeat conversion. If the market had fully priced a costly outcome, the implied move and put demand would sit far above the name's history. The put OI is extreme (P/C 37.8), but the implied move of 12.0% is within the 13.9% max reaction.
evidence.independence: The Record, 2026-10-30, https://therecord.media/resolve-fashion-retailer-data-breach-payment-cards, reports the same incident with state counts (Texas 127,200, Vermont 1,328). It rests on the same company disclosure. No law-firm investigation was found.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue should land near the bar. July net sales were +18% y/y (company), and consensus $344.8M implies +16.6% against an easy Q3 2025 comp (+4.4%). The last two quarters' first-month figures were +16% (first 7 weeks of Q1, Q1 landed +16%) and +14% (April, Q2 landed +12%), so a ~2-point fade from July lands at about $343M, inside the bar. On a two-year stack, Q3 consensus (~21%) equals Q2's (~21-22%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $347.4M beat (+12%), and the stock fell -4.06%. Q1 2026: +16% revenue, April +14%, and the stock fell -13.87%. Q3 2025: revenue missed (+4.4%) on a margin beat, and the stock rose +11.01%. Revenue has not decided this stock's direction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus already embeds the July +18% with a shade of fade. The only unpriced part is how much Aug-Sep slowed or held, which no free traffic or card series covers for 2026.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526206442/rvlv-ex99_1.htm, April +14% leading to Q2 +12%) gives the fade pattern. That is a different document but the same company.

evidence.text: The Q3 gross-margin guide of 53.5-54.0% (-88bp y/y at the midpoint, explained by a tough comp) looks conservative. Underlying Q2 GM excluding refunds was ~55.0% against a 54.1-54.6% guide, about 40-90bp above the top. Separately, the CFO said $1.4M of further IEEPA refund claims were 'not received or included in our financials or guidance', worth roughly 40bp of Q3 GM if received in the quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: a margin-led beat on a sales miss bought +11.01%. Q2 2026: a 56.6% GM against a 54.1-54.6% guide (refund-aided) still fell -4.06%. Margin beats have paid once and been sold once.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sell side knows the company beats its GM guide. The $1.4M refund is a one-off and too small to matter much (~$0.015 EPS). If the market expected a clear GM beat, EPS consensus would sit above the guide-implied ~$0.21. The two EPS sources disagree ($0.21 against $0.23), so this is capped small.
evidence.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526332838/rvlv-ex99_1.htm) carries the 162bp refund benefit and the 54.1-54.6% prior guide. This is the same company's documents and the same event.

evidence.text: Opex has run over guidance two quarters running, and the forward guide is the line this stock sells on. Q2 marketing was 16.5% of sales against a 15.7% guide, S&D was 17.9% ('slightly above our guidance range') and G&A was 'slightly above plan'. FY marketing was raised to 15.8-16.0% and G&A to $170-172M. Q4 marketing is pre-flagged 'north of 16%', and growth initiatives cost ~2 points of adjusted EBITDA margin in 2026. A Q3 overshoot of the 15.0% marketing guide, or a 2027 investment signal, is the likeliest negative on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (marketing 15.8% against 14.3% the prior year, Los Angeles label investment): -13.87% on an EPS beat. Q2 2026 (marketing raised, G&A raised): -4.06% on an EPS beat of $0.26 against $0.20. The baseline shows 1 up of 7 reactions.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q4 marketing step-up is already public. What is not public is whether Q3 overran again and how management frames 2027 investment. If this were fully priced, the stock would not have fallen on two consecutive EPS beats. The pattern is an inference from two quarters, not a document about Q3.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526206442/rvlv-ex99_1.htm): marketing 15.8% against 14.3%. AAII (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/527118-what-you-need-to-know-about-revolve-group-incs-q3-earnings): 2 EPS estimate cuts and 0 raises in the last month. That is a different source pointing the same way on profit.

evidence.text: Sell-side targets were trimmed into the print, but ratings held. Raymond James cut its target from $28 to $25 (2026-10-16, Buy) and UBS from $29 to $27 (2026-10-27, Hold). Roth ($37, 10-21), Stifel ($33, 10-28) and BTIG ($35, 10-28) maintained or reiterated Buy. EPS revisions ran 2 down and 0 up over the month. A lowered bar slightly raises the odds that an in-line quarter is not sold.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Before Q2 2026 targets were not cut, and the stock fell -4.06%.
evidence.why_not_priced: These are public, so largely priced. The marginal point is that expectations drifted lower into the print rather than higher, which is the opposite of the Q1 and Q2 setups.
evidence.independence: AAII revision count (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/527118-what-you-need-to-know-about-revolve-group-incs-q3-earnings), a different source. It overlaps with finding 4 on the revisions datum, which is used here only as evidence of a lowered bar.
